validated_results.title: Plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D and prostate cancer risk: the multiethnic cohort.
validated_results.reason: Nested case-control study within a prospective multiethnic cohort reporting plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations and risk of incident prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: Plasma 25(OH)D <20 ng/ml versus 30-<50 ng/ml (clinically defined cutpoints)
extraction.ethnicity: African American, Native Hawaiian, Japanese, Latino and White

sample_size.excerpt: The purpose of this study was to examine the relationship of plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) concentrations to prostate cancer within a large multiethnic cohort in Hawaii and California using a nested case-control design. The study included 329 incidents of prostate cancer of African American, Native Hawaiian, Japanese, Latino and White ancestry, and 656 controls matched on age, race/ethnicity, date/time of blood collection and fasting status.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 329 + 656 = 985

cases.excerpt: The study included 329 incidents of prostate cancer of African American, Native Hawaiian, Japanese, Latino and White ancestry, and 656 controls matched on age, race/ethnicity, date/time of blood collection and fasting status.

effect_size.excerpt: When clinically defined cutpoints were used, there was no increased risk for the lowest 25(OH)D concentration (OR for <20 versus 30-<50ng/ml=1.10, 95% CI=0.68-1.78), while there was a suggestive increased risk for higher concentrations (OR for 50ng/ml=1.52, 95% CI=0.92-2.51).

validated_results.title: The association of plasma fatty acids with prostate cancer risk in Nigerians.
validated_results.reason: Original case-control analysis in Nigerian men reporting plasma docosapentaenoic acid quartile odds ratios for prostate cancer risk.

extraction.population: Men aged 40 years or older recruited from surgery/urology clinics and rural and urban communities

sample_size.excerpt: Mean ages for 66 (22.6%) cases and 226 (77.4%) controls were 71.9+/-11.47 and 56.7+/-12.69 years, P<.001, and median (25th, 75th percentile) fasting plasma FA were 2,447 (2,087, 3,024) and 2,373 (2,014, 2,751) microg/mL, respectively.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 66 + 226 = 292

cases.excerpt: Mean ages for 66 (22.6%) cases and 226 (77.4%) controls were 71.9+/-11.47 and 56.7+/-12.69 years, P<.001, and median (25th, 75th percentile) fasting plasma FA were 2,447 (2,087, 3,024) and 2,373 (2,014, 2,751) microg/mL, respectively.

effect_size.excerpt: Unadjusted ORQ2vs.Q1 for omega-3 FAs eicosapentaenoic (EPA) and docosapentaenoic (DPA) were 0.39 (95% CI, 0.18-0.85) and 0.79 (95% CI, 0.35-1.79) respectively. In this population with high total plasma omega-3, we observed modest positive PCa risk trend with total plasma omega-6 (2.3), inverse risk reduction with EPA (0.4), and strong positive risk associations with behenic (2.8), erucic (4.2), and nervonic (2.4) acids.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Unadjusted ORQ2vs.Q1 for omega-3 FAs eicosapentaenoic (EPA) and docosapentaenoic (DPA) were 0.39 (95% CI, 0.18-0.85) and 0.79 (95% CI, 0.35-1.79) respectively.

design.excerpt: Odds ratio (OR) of PCa risk was determined by unconditional logistic regression with the plasma FA 1st quartile as reference
